# OTIO reference fixture

`cuts.otio` and the downgraded `cuts-v1.otio` are generated by `generate.py` using the official
[OpenTimelineIO 0.18.1](https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/OpenTimelineIO/tree/v0.18.1)
Python package. The generator does not import Codeboard.

The video track places shot B before shot A. B has 60 source frames at 30 fps,
trimmed to `[6, 36)`. A has 48 frames at 24 fps with media origin 1001, trimmed
to `[1007, 1025)`. The resulting edit occupies 42 frames at 24 fps. Display
names are deliberately present so import must reject or report their omission.

Regenerate in an environment with `opentimelineio==0.18.1`:

```sh
python test/fixtures/otio/generate.py
```

`verify.py <study-export.otio> <reserialized.otio>` checks the documentation
study's export with that same official package: both source ranges, media URLs,
stable IDs, cut position and total duration. It reserializes the result for a
second Codeboard import. Python/OTIO are reference-fixture tools, not runtime
dependencies of Codeboard or its TypeScript studies.
